who: Historian of women, labour and health care at Memorial University and the University of New Brunswick; doctorate in history from Toronto.

evidence.says: UNB describes her Toronto education and history dissertation, earlier professorship and department headship at Memorial, move to UNB in April 2002, and PhD supervision at both universities.
The 2015 emerita citation says Linda Kealey arrived in 2002 and supervised five UNB doctoral students to completion.
Identifies Linda Kealey as Memorial history department head and lists A Not Unreasonable Claim among her publications.
LC identifies Linda Kealey through A Not Unreasonable Claim (1979).

notes: Matching book connects the authority record to the historian whose appointments and doctoral supervision agree with the AHA institutions.

who: Historian of twentieth-century US women and gender at UNC Greensboro; history PhD, Wisconsin-Madison, 2002.

evidence.says: Hannah Grace Dudley Shotwell’s 2016 UNCG doctoral dissertation identifies Dr. Lisa Levenstein as committee chair.
Stephen Kantrowitz’s Wisconsin-Madison CV lists Lisa Levenstein, PhD 2002, UNC Greensboro, among history doctoral graduates on whose committees he served.
Levenstein identifies herself as UNCG professor of history, specializing in twentieth-century US women and gender, and author of A Movement Without Marches.
LC identifies Lisa Levenstein as the author of A Movement Without Marches (2009).

notes: Direct supervision evidence, matching doctorate and shared book establish the match.

who: University of Maine historian of US labour and foreign relations; PhD, Northwestern, 1987.

evidence.says: Maine identifies Elizabeth McKillen as history professor emerita, describes her graduate teaching in labour and foreign relations, and lists Chicago Labor and the Quest for a Democratic Diplomacy.
The 2008 H-Diplo contributor biography identifies McKillen as a University of Maine history professor, author of Chicago Labor, and recipient of a Northwestern PhD in 1987.
LC identifies Elizabeth McKillen through Chicago Labor and the Quest for a Democratic Diplomacy, 1914–1924 (1995).

notes: Institution during the supervision period, doctorate and distinctive publication agree.

who: Louise Michele Newman, University of Florida historian of US women, gender and culture; PhD, Brown, 1992.

evidence.says: Florida gives Louise Newman’s Brown PhD (1992), appointment at Florida from 1993, and editorship of Men’s Ideas/Women’s Realities: Popular Science, 1870–1915.
The department’s PhD alumni directory lists Jessica Lancia’s dissertation, Gloria Steinem: the Transnational Life of an American Feminist, with Louise Newman as advisor.
LC’s heading is Newman, Louise Michele; its source is Men’s Ideas/Women’s Realities, with Louise Michele Newman on the title page.

notes: The shared edited volume links the expanded authority name to the Florida supervisor; Brown 1992 also matches.

who: Donald Lee Parman, Purdue historian of twentieth-century Native American history.

evidence.says: Purdue’s Donald Lee Parman authority entry identifies him as a history professor specializing in twentieth-century Native American history, appointed in 1966 and later professor emeritus.
The publisher identifies Donald L. Parman, author of Indians and the American West in the Twentieth Century (1994), as professor of history at Purdue.
LC identifies Donald Lee Parman through The Indian Civil Conservation Corps and Indians and the American West in the Twentieth Century, gives Donald L. Parman as a variant, and links Q112391139.

notes: Purdue affiliation, full-name authority heading, publication and Native American specialization establish the candidate identity.

who: James Earl Sherow, Kansas State historian of environmental, Kansas and western US history; PhD, Colorado, 1987.

evidence.says: K-State’s 2020 retirement notice gives appointment in 1992, Colorado history doctorate in 1987, dissertation Watering the Valley, and service as major advisor to six doctoral graduates.
Lists James Sherow with Colorado PhD (1987), environmental, Kansas and western US history, and retirement in spring 2020.
LC identifies James Earl Sherow through Watering the Valley (1990), records James E. Sherow as another usage, and links Q112446885.

notes: Matching doctorate, university tenure covering the students, and distinctive work link James Sherow to the expanded authority name.

who: Michigan State historian of Native American history and the Great Lakes; doctorate from the University of Michigan.

evidence.says: MSU’s 2025 tribute describes her Michigan doctorate and MSU career through retirement in 2021, explicitly calls Joseph Genetin-Pilawa a PhD student, and discusses her mentorship of Aaron Luedtke.
The publisher names Susan Sleeper Smith as a coeditor of New Faces of the Fur Trade (1998) and identifies her as a Michigan State history professor.
LC identifies Susan Sleeper-Smith through New Faces of the Fur Trade (1998).

notes: Named doctoral students and matching university agree with AHA; the coedited volume connects the LC identity.

who: Columbia historian of twentieth-century American foreign relations and historical theory; PhD, Columbia, 1986.

evidence.says: Columbia identifies Anders Stephanson as professor emeritus of history, gives Columbia PhD (1986), and lists Kennan and the Art of Foreign Policy (1989).
Benjamin Coates’s CV gives his Columbia American history PhD in 2010 and lists teaching-assistant work for Anders Stephanson’s Columbia course on US foreign relations.
LC identifies Anders Stephanson through Kennan and the Art of Foreign Policy (1989).

notes: The doctorate, Columbia affiliation in a listed student’s period, field and identical book establish the match.
